properties.name: The registry closes designs nobody is using, reuses the least recently used slot when full, and says busy (503) instead of not found
properties.rationale:
req:a-hosted-server-closes-idle-designs-and-says-busy-when-full, on @ajs's word ("Yes, let's build the now items in reflow2"). Before this, an opened design stayed open until the process ended, so the open-design limit was a budget for the process lifetime. flo2.io met it on 2026-09-27 (fact:flo2-io-met-the-open-design-cap-with-no-idle-eviction-2026-09-27).

THE GUARD THAT MATTERED MOST WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. With the release wait removed, the reopen test failed with RocksDB's own error: "IO error: lock hold by current process". A request still streaming an answer can hold the old copy after the router lets go, and a naive reopen then collides with its own process.

The other guards were also observed failing:
- With LRU reuse replaced by refusal, the full-server test fails.
- The first version of the --registry-idle flag panicked the binary on every launch. clap reads an Option<T> field as "optional T", and the parser returned Option<Duration>. The existing transport test caught it, and the flag now parses to a plain Duration with 0 as never.

NOT IN IT: a shared memory budget across open stores, and draining on shutdown. Both are on epoch:planned-the-hosted-engine-closes-idle-designs-and-drains.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
registry_http.rs gives each design a slot that tracks its last use and its requests in progress.
- A background sweep closes designs idle past --registry-idle (default 15m; 0 never). So does any request that finds the table full.
- At --registry-max-open, the least recently used design with nothing in flight is closed to make room.
- Refusals map to statuses: an unknown id is 404; every slot busy, or a store that would not open, is 503 with Retry-After. It used to be 404 for everything.
- Closing ends every session on the design.
- A reopen waits on a Weak to the old copy's store until nothing holds it, so the same process never opens one store twice.
- A failed open is remembered for 30 s, not forever.
- An id that names no design is resolved before it takes a place, so it can never push a real design out.
New flag: --registry-idle.
